title: Galleria Borghese: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works in which physical contact carries much of the story.
introduction:
Bernini's Proserpina twists away from the arms lifting her. Raphael's bearers coordinate their movements around the weight of the dead Christ. In both works, the relation between bodies explains the action before every participant has been named. Looking at contact offers an immediate route into subjects that can otherwise arrive burdened with mythology or doctrine.

The selection also includes portraits, a concert and figures assuming classical roles. Here the body's task may be to present rather than struggle. Keep the individual objects distinct: the *Apollo and Daphne* below is Dosso Dossi's painting, not Bernini's sculpture. Shared titles and familiar stories can conceal important differences in medium, episode and point of view.
visitNote: These selected works belong to the Borghese collection; loans and room arrangements can change. Consult the museum’s official booking and collection pages before visiting. Dosso Dossi’s Apollo and Daphne in this guide is a painting, distinct from Bernini’s sculpture of the same subject.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: The sections on movement and the disposition of figures offer a starting point for comparing the effort in Raphael’s bearers with the supported, twisting bodies in Bernini’s sculpture.

works.title: Apollo and Daphne
works.credit: Dosso Dossi. Apollo and Daphne. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Dosso Dossi places the music-making Apollo close to the viewer, while the pursuit involving Daphne unfolds farther back. The painting separates activities that its title may lead us to expect in one immediate encounter. Attention has to travel between foreground performance and distant narrative. The landscape is part of that separation, not merely scenery behind a single action.

works.title: The Abduction of Proserpina
works.credit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini. The Rape of Proserpina. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Pluto's upward grip meets Proserpina's twisting resistance and her hand against his face. Bernini makes opposing forces occupy one sculptural group. The apparent indentation of the thigh under his fingers adds another contradiction: hard marble describes yielding flesh. Technical virtuosity should not eclipse the subject's coercion; the material effect makes the physical pressure more legible.

works.title: Sacred and Profane Love
works.credit: Titian. Sacred and Profane Love. Image credit: Titian; Source credit: Galleria Borghese. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: Similar faces and different states of dress connect the two women while setting them apart. Between them, Cupid's hand enters the water. The familiar title does not close the interpretative problem: the museum discusses a range of readings and favours a marital context. Begin with the pairing before assigning one figure a simple moral superiority over the other.

works.title: Boy with a Basket of Fruit
works.catalogueTitle: Boy with a Basket of Fruit
works.credit: Caravaggio. Boy with a Basket of Fruit. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The basket reaches forward, bringing fruit, leaves and face into a shared claim on attention. Caravaggio does not leave still life as a minor accessory to a portrait. The young man's turned body and slipping shirt establish an encounter in which the held objects occupy much of the available space between figure and viewer.

works.title: Sick Bacchus
works.credit: Caravaggio. Young Sick Bacchus. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Ivy and grapes identify a classical role carried by an unidealised young body. The turn over the bare shoulder gives the figure a constrained relation to the table and fruit. Pale flesh is available for observation, but a painted appearance cannot establish a medical diagnosis. The familiar title should not be allowed to substitute for evidence about illness.

works.title: Madonna of the Palafrenieri
works.catalogueTitle: Madonna and Child with St. Anne
works.credit: Madonna and Child with St. Anne. WikiArt; Caravaggio. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Mary steadies the child as a small foot presses against the serpent; the older woman watches. Caravaggio makes the religious action depend on shared balance and pressure. Three generations occupy the dark setting, distinguished by strong light and bodily scale. The smallest figure carries the decisive action while remaining physically dependent on support.

works.title: Marcello Sacchetti
works.credit: Pietro da Cortona. Marcello Sacchetti. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pietro-da-cortona/marcello-sacchetti
works.description: White lace interrupts the black clothing at collar and cuff, directing attention towards face and hand. An architectural support gives the standing figure a formal setting. Pietro da Cortona allows public presentation to emerge through controlled bearing and material distinction. The portrait's display is distributed across dress and pose rather than concentrated in an overtly dramatic gesture.

works.title: Saint Jerome Writing
works.credit: Caravaggio. Saint Jerome. Image credit: Caravaggio; Source credit: Self-scanned. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The bare arm stretches across the table towards the work, creating a long illuminated connection through the dark setting. At the other end, the skull introduces mortality into the same working space. Caravaggio does not separate intellectual labour from the vulnerable body performing it. Writing is made visible as an effort sustained by an ageing person.

works.title: Minerva Dressing
works.credit: Lavinia Fontana. Minerva Dressing. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Armour and helmet identify Minerva even when they are not being worn. Lavinia Fontana presents the goddess in an interval of dressing, with the turned body reaching towards clothing. Role and costume are briefly separated. The surrounding objects preserve the mythological identity while the action reveals the practical transition into its familiar appearance.

works.title: Cupid and Psyche
works.credit: Jacopo Zucchi. Amor and Psyche. Image credit: Jacopo Zucchi. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The raised lamp makes looking the decisive action. Psyche approaches the sleeping Cupid through a crowded setting of flowers, fabric and pale bodies. Zucchi gives illumination a narrative function: it permits a discovery while exposing the act that produces it. The light belongs to someone's decision inside the scene rather than arriving as an unexplained theatrical effect.

works.title: The Deposition
works.catalogueTitle: Deposition (The Carrying of the Dead Christ to the Sepulchre)
works.credit: Raphael. Deposition (The Carrying of the Dead Christ to the Sepulchre). Image credit: Raphael; Source credit: aiwaz.net. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The bearers must coordinate opposing steps around Christ's weight. Nearby, a collapsing mourner creates another need for support. Raphael joins these actions within a group whose grief is inseparable from bodily effort. The dead body and the faltering living figure require different responses, giving the composition more than one centre of physical dependence.

works.title: Saint John the Baptist
works.credit: Bronzino. Saint John the Baptist. Image credit: Bronzino. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Bronzino twists the torso across the rocky seat while the pointing arm establishes another direction. Blue cloth distinguishes the exposed body without resolving its complicated pose. The saint is presented through bodily arrangement rather than a fully narrated episode. Following the different axes of arm and torso explains the figure's activity before the gesture's religious significance is added.

works.title: Self-Portrait as a Mature Man
works.catalogueTitle: Self Portrait of Gianlorenzo Bernini as a Mature Man (1638-40)
works.credit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini. Self Portrait of Gianlorenzo Bernini as a Mature Man (1638-40). Image credit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Light gathers around Bernini's eyes and cheek, while a small white collar interrupts the dark clothing. The surrounding marks are economical enough to leave the face in command. Compared with his sculptural groups, this painted self-presentation requires little overt action. Its immediacy is constructed through selective emphasis rather than a narrative event.

works.title: Self-Portrait as a Young Man
works.catalogueTitle: Self Portrait of Gianlorenzo Bernini as young man (1623)
works.credit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini. Self Portrait of Gianlorenzo Bernini as young man (1623). Image credit: Gian Lorenzo Bernini. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The turned head directs attention differently from the body beneath its broad collar. Dark hair and shadow frame the eyes, making their orientation conspicuous. Comparing the two Bernini self-portraits can begin with these modest changes of pose and illumination. There is no need to read a complete account of youth or maturity into either expression.

works.title: The Taking of Christ
works.credit: Dirck van Baburen. The Capture of Jesus Christ. Image credit: Dirck van Baburen. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The narrow dark space makes faces and armour seem to obstruct one another. Baburen selects parts of the arrest through reflected light while leaving other contacts difficult to disentangle. The lack of room is consequential. It turns the event into a close bodily encounter rather than allowing a detached view of neatly separated participants.

works.title: The Concert
works.credit: Gerard van Honthorst. The Concert. Image credit: Gerard van Honthorst. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Open music gives the crowded company a shared reference point, but their attention moves between page and companions. Honthorst distinguishes the tasks of playing, reading and listening inside the compact group. Feathered hats extend its silhouette above the table. The concert is visible as coordination among different actions rather than as one repeated musician's pose.

works.title: Saint John the Baptist
works.credit: Caravaggio. Saint John the Baptist. Image credit: Caravaggio; Source credit: Self-scanned. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: Caravaggio's seated figure offers a marked contrast with Bronzino's twisting saint. Dropped shoulders and partly extended legs make inactivity conspicuous beside the red cloth and nearby ram. Traditional signs identify John without dictating an energetic prophetic pose. The exposed body and its slack arrangement deserve attention before an emotional explanation is assigned to the young face.

works.title: Madonna and Child with the Infant Saint John
works.catalogueTitle: Virgin and Child with the Infant Saint John the Baptist
works.credit: Lorenzo di Credi. Virgin and Child with the Infant Saint John the Baptist. Image credit: Lorenzo di Credi. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The circular boundary gathers several directions of attention around Mary's upright figure. Lorenzo di Credi lets the children's differing poses animate that enclosure without breaking the group's closeness. The landscape offers another space behind them. The round format is an active constraint on how bodies and their gestures can fit together.

works.title: Adoration of the Child
works.credit: Fra Bartolomeo. Adoration of the Child. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The child lies low, requiring the adults' bodies to bend towards the ground. Fra Bartolomeo organises their attention into a broad triangular relation inside the circular panel. Ruins and landscape remain behind the group, but the immediate action is a lowering of bodies. The smallest figure determines the others' posture despite occupying little space.

works.title: David with the Head of Goliath
works.catalogueTitle: David Contemplating the Head of Goliath
works.credit: Orazio Gentileschi. David Contemplating the Head of Goliath. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Orazio Gentileschi chooses an interval after the struggle. David looks down towards the severed head, his body now comparatively settled against the dark tree. Pale cloth and limbs keep him distinct without reenacting the battle. The painting presents a result and an act of attention, leaving the preceding violence to be reconstructed from what remains.

closingSections.title: Compare before naming a mood
paragraphs: The two Saint Johns and the two Bernini self-portraits offer especially useful comparisons of posture. Keep artists and object identities attached to their titles. Check current access and displays with the gallery; this selection is not a timed route through its rooms.
